answer: Admission should be paced by the beacon. A fixed quota of new identities clears per epoch; a gale of same-shaped registrations stretches the queue, so a botnet's n clones wait n paced rounds before earning — capital cannot buy parallel entry. Purses are tournaments: fixed prizes to top-ranked answers, not pro-rata drips, so extra clones only deepen a contest they must win. At each close, auditors re-execute one random canyon of the ledger, calibrated to the yarrow baseline of honest work; a cloned lineage that fails forfeits its share. Attackers pay in time, competition, and audit risk.
